messages:
adele: Heads up — saw a couple latency blips this morning in us-west1 when spot nodes were reclaimed. p95 jumped ~300ms for stable chat sessions :grimacing:

michael_s: ugh, thanks. any pattern on which instance types?

jun: looks like it was mostly g5x2 preemptions around 07:12-07:22, sudden drop in available slots triggered routing thrash.

tara_ops: were long-lived sessions pinned to spot? that's the usual pain point.

adele: yep — a handful of multi-turn (>=30 reqs) user sessions were still on spot lanes. autoscaler tried to reschedule but KV cache warmup added ~200ms each.

michael_s: proposal: enforce a region-level min on-demand floor for sessions > 20 requests or >60s active. prevents warm restarts for heavy sessions. :thumbsup:

jun: agree. also think we should implement a spot "drip warmup" — keep a tiny warm pool of spot nodes that get recycled into burst lanes gradually instead of full drain. that reduces cold-kv penalties.

tara_ops: can we combine with eviction credits so tenants that consume burst get charged credits first? means we ration burst consumption during prolonged drains.

adele: I sketched a config idea, quick YAML: ```
mixed_pool:
  min_on_demand_floor_pct: 12  # per-region baseline
  session_thresholds:
    long_session_requests: 20
    long_session_seconds: 60
  spot_warmup:
    warm_pool_size_pct: 3
    drip_rate_per_min: 2  # nodes/min to move into burst pool
  eviction_credit_policy:
    refill_rate_per_min: 1
    max_credits_per_tenant: 30
```

michael_s: numbers look sane, but 12% floor might be expensive in small regions. can we do a sliding floor based on region capacity? e.g., min(12%, max(5%, 200 GPUs / region_capacity * 100))

jun: yeah, use absolute min GPUs too. small regions get a 4 GPU hard floor, otherwise % looks weird.

tara_ops: ops question — how do we handle model-variant fallback during reclaim? we could route to a smaller quantized variant to keep latency low while using less memory. that helps when on-demand capacity is saturated.

adele: plan: primary fallback is same-model quantized variant (if available) + route sticky sessions to on-demand. secondary fallback is regional reroute to nearest healthy region (with user-consent or default policy).

infra-bot: Deploy-check: a/b rollout of floor config recommended. start with 10% of traffic in us-west1, observe p95 and cost delta for 48h.

michael_s: simulation ran locally — expected cost increase ~3.6% for us-west1 at 12% floor, but predicted p95 improvement ~120ms and session error drop of 0.8%. tradeoff ok for SLA workloads.

jun: also we should add quick preempt hooks to checkpoint KV cache every N tokens for long sessions so moving to on-demand doesn't restart generation. cheap snapshots reduce warmup.

tara_ops: can someone estimate burst pool wasted cycles? naive calc: warm_pool 3% + drip -> maybe 0.6% extra runtime waste if utilization steady. we can amortize by making warm nodes serve low-priority batches.

adele: next steps: 1) run regional sim with sliding-floor + 4-GPU floor for small regions (jun) 2) infra-job to implement spot_warmup/drip (michael_s) 3) add checkpoint hook RFC for KV snapshots (tara_ops) 4) A/B rollout via infra-bot (adele)

michael_s: I'll spin a test branch, will include metrics (eviction_count, session_migrations, p95 by session-length, cost delta).

jun: tagging @oncall for visibility when we roll, but happy with the plan.

tara_ops: thumbs up. prefer to start in staging -> ap-southeast-1 -> then us-west1.

adele: thanks all. will update the runbook and link the RFC here when ready. :rocket:
